claim: In September 2026, the youth unemployment rate in the EU-27 was 15.5% (people under 25, seasonally adjusted).
In 2025, one in four young people in Spain were unemployed (24.9%).
Of the ten countries, Germany had the lowest youth unemployment rate in September 2026: 7.5%.
In September 2026, youth unemployment in Romania was 30.8%.
Youth unemployment in Czechia fell from 11.8% in August 2026 to 8.9% in September 2026, because of a new national training programme.

Bell and Blanchflower (2011), 'Young people and the Great Recession', Oxford Review of Economic Policy, https://doi.org/10.1093/oxrep/grr008, show that young people lost jobs faster than older people.
In September 2026, the youth unemployment rate in Sweden (21.7%) was higher than in Italy (19.9%).
